body:
Recent local benchmark update — 2026-10-21

These runs used an **uncommitted local follow-up** to this PR, not the published PR head (`bc78b774`). The retained follow-up source archive has SHA-256 `c610fb0ef60cea93f8e28184bee7da8f86398545cd6e48d272c0f958e4e45765`. No changes have been committed or pushed.

Home-lab: M1 Pro, 10 physical cores / 32 GiB, Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, PostgreSQL 18. All load generators ran on this same physical machine. These are colocated ARM lab measurements, not an official challenge score or a dedicated eight-physical-core server maximum.

- **4-vCPU server allocation:** server + PostgreSQL restricted to CPUs 0–3 in a 10-vCPU / 16-GiB VM; four generators on CPUs 4–9 in that VM.
- **8-vCPU server allocation:** fresh server VM with 8 vCPUs / 16 GiB; four generators sharing a separate 4-vCPU / 4-GiB VM on the same host, connected through Lima user-v2.

Each hold used a fresh full-seed clone (500,000 articles / 100,000 accounts), think-scale 1, a 60-second ramp, 300-second measurement and 15-second tail. SLO limits: p95 <500 ms, p99 <1000 ms, errors <1%, with separate generator-headroom, lag and clock-validity checks. Users below mean concurrent simulated VUs, not requests/s or GitHub contributors.

| Local revision / allocation | Concurrent VUs | Hold | Successful requests/s | p95 ms | p99 ms | Errors | Overall qualification |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Retained follow-up / 4 vCPUs | 80,000 | 1 | 20,801.81 | 356.607 | 442.879 | 0% | PASS |
| Retained follow-up / 4 vCPUs | 80,000 | 2 | 20,833.09 | 317.695 | 391.935 | 0% | PASS |
| Retained follow-up / 4 vCPUs | 96,000 | 1 valid trial | 20,784.12 | 718.335 | 771.071 | 7.6342% | FAIL |
| Experimental idle-writer borrowing / 4 vCPUs | 96,000 | 1 | 20,637.48 | 737.791 | 794.623 | 7.6783% | FAIL; experiment reverted |
| Retained follow-up / 8 vCPUs | 96,000 | 1 | 25,422.95 | 9.423 | 18.991 | 0% | **INVALID; native SLO PASS is diagnostic only** |

The 8-vCPU hold completed 7,626,886 measured requests. All four shards had 24,000 active VUs at measurement-window start, no generator lag, approximately 46.4% whole-generator-VM average CPU, and valid clock witnesses. However, a custom host Pageouts check increased from 212,219,172 to 212,222,569, invalidating the trial under its predeclared rule. This is not a Rust capacity failure, and the native SLO pass is **not counted as a qualifying pass**. The pageout-only rule is a conservative custom exclusion, not proof of guest swapping; no continuous host-memory witness was collected. The earlier network setup attempt also remains INVALID and never started warmup load.

The retained follow-up passed 32 native release tests (one helper ignored) and 197/197 official conformance steps on each of the dev and full seeds. Both live seed fingerprints and frozen source/binary hashes were verified. The separate borrowing experiment was reverted after failing to establish an improvement; it is not in the retained follow-up.

**Current repeat-validated result: 80,000 concurrent VUs at the 4-vCPU server allocation. No eight-vCPU level has two qualifying passes.** No second eight-vCPU 96k hold, 128k, 160k or higher hold ran. Invalid and historical trials do not advance the two-pass ladder. Above 100k VUs, the workload would reuse the 100k seeded accounts, so VUs must be distinguished from unique identities.

Owned benchmark processes were cleaned up and the paused home-lab workloads restored. Raw results, clocks, source hashes and restoration evidence are retained locally.

body:
### Updated local benchmark results (2026-10-21)

Follow-up to the [earlier benchmark comment](https://github.com/arjaythedev/multicore-server-challenge/pull/11#issuecomment-6310454581). These runs use the **uncommitted local follow-up**, not the published PR head. Frozen source archive SHA256: `c610fb0ef60cea93f8e28184bee7da8f86398545cd6e48d272c0f958e4e45765`.

**Setup:** server VM 8 vCPUs / 16 GiB; generators in a separate 4-vCPU VM on the **same physical home-lab** (M1 Pro, 10 physical cores / 32 GiB). Generator RAM is listed per row. Rust and PostgreSQL share the server CPU budget. This is a colocated allocation result, not an official challenge score or dedicated eight-core maximum.

| Concurrent VUs | Generator RAM | Run | Verdict | Successful requests/s | p95 | p99 | Errors |
|---:|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 96,000 | 4 GiB | u96000-1 | PASS (hold) | 25405.33 | 10.351 ms | 20.559 ms | 0.0000% |
| 96,000 | 4 GiB | u96000-2 | PASS (hold) | 25409.17 | 9.335 ms | 18.703 ms | 0.0000% |
| 128,000 | 4 GiB | u128000-1 | INVALID (hold) | — | — ms | — ms | — |
| 128,000 | 8 GiB | u128000-1 | FAIL (hold) | 29153.41 | 2096.127 ms | 10002.431 ms | 2.9351% |

Highest level with two qualifying passes: 96,000 concurrent simulated users.

The fresh 8-GiB-generator 128k hold failed the native SLOs: 147,160 HTTP 503 responses and 117,309 request timeouts (264,469 errors / 9,010,492 requests). Host and guest memory checks passed. The ladder stopped. No second 128k hold with 8 GiB generators ran; no 160k or higher run was attempted. This is a result for the combined colocated system; it does not isolate the Rust application as the sole bottleneck.

The 4-GiB generator VM recorded four OOM kills at 128k; that hold is invalid and does not establish a Rust capacity limit. The retry uses 8 GiB for the generator VM with the server, frozen binaries, workload and validity criteria unchanged.

Each arm uses a fresh full seed (500k articles / 100k accounts), think-scale 1; 300-VU warmup, >=75s drain, then a 60s ramp and 300s scored window. PASS requires p95 <500 ms, p99 <1000 ms, errors <1%, all VUs active at measurement-window start and valid generator CPU, lag, ports, clocks and guest memory checks.

The corrected prospective host check requires sampled normal pressure, no new compressor swapouts and complete nominal 1-Hz evidence (gaps <=3s). Pageouts and swapins are diagnostic. Earlier invalid trials remain excluded; sampling can miss brief pressure changes.

VUs mean concurrent simulated users, not requests/s or contributors. Above 100k VUs, the workload reuses the 100k seeded identities. Preparation passed 32 release tests (1 ignored), both 197-step conformance suites, both seed fingerprints and source/input/binary hashes.

Raw shard validation confirmed all four 32k-VU populations at measurement-window start, no generator lag, generator-VM average CPU about 45.5%, valid clock witnesses and no port/descriptor exhaustion. The saved native assessment recomputes identically.

Raw evidence and checksums are retained locally. Workloads and VM states were restored. **No commits or pushes.**
